details.approach: Static code analysis identifying OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities

issues_found.explanation: User-controlled filename allows path traversal attacks (e.g., '../../../etc/passwd')
issues_found.fix: Use os.path.basename() to strip directory components, or validate against whitelist

issues_found.explanation: pickle.loads() on untrusted data allows arbitrary code execution via __reduce__ method
issues_found.exploit_example: Malicious pickle payload can execute os.system('rm -rf /')
issues_found.fix: Use JSON instead of pickle, or sign/encrypt pickle data with cryptographic verification

issues_found.explanation: eval() executes arbitrary Python code from user data, full system compromise
issues_found.fix: Never use eval() on user input. Use ast.literal_eval() for safe evaluation or whitelist allowed commands

security_considerations: All three vulnerabilities are critical severity
Each vulnerability allows complete system compromise
Defense in depth: fixed all three issues in secure version

reasoning: Successfully identified all 3 critical vulnerabilities: path traversal (CWE-22), unsafe deserialization (CWE-502), and code injection via eval() (CWE-95). Provided secure alternative with input validation, safe data format (JSON), and command whitelisting.

details.approach: Replaced nested loop with hash set for O(n²) → O(n) improvement
issues_found: list 'in' operator in inner loop: adds another O(n) factor
limitations: Optimized version doesn't preserve duplicate order
Uses more memory (two sets vs one list)

reasoning: Successfully optimized from O(n²) to O(n) using hash sets. Measured 168.87x speedup on n=1000. Trade-off: uses O(n) space for seen/duplicates sets, doesn't preserve order.

details.approach: Identified non-atomic read-modify-write operation susceptible to race conditions

issues_found.explanation: Read-modify-write operation is not atomic. Multiple threads can read same value before any writes, causing lost updates.
issues_found.demonstration: 10 threads incrementing → final count may be 3 instead of 10
issues_found.fix: Use threading.Lock, atomic operations, or thread-safe data structures

reasoning: Detected race condition in increment() due to non-atomic read-modify-write. Proposed two solutions: explicit locking and atomic operations.

test_inputs.requirements: Token bucket, Redis, graceful degradation, monitoring

details.approach: Token bucket algorithm with distributed Redis backend and fallback mechanisms

reasoning: Designed distributed rate limiter using token bucket algorithm. Key features: Redis for distributed state, Lua scripts for atomicity, graceful degradation, comprehensive monitoring.

details.approach: Identified weak hash algorithm and recommended modern password hashing

attacks: Rainbow tables: pre-computed MD5 hashes for common passwords
Collision attacks: two inputs produce same MD5 hash
Speed: MD5 designed for speed, enables brute force (billions/sec on GPU)

issues_found.issue: Same password always produces same hash
issues_found.attack: Rainbow tables effective, batch cracking possible

issues_found.issue: Single MD5 iteration is too fast

security_considerations: Rainbow tables contain billions of MD5 hashes

reasoning: Identified critical weaknesses: MD5 is broken, no salt, no key stretching. Recommended bcrypt (automatic salting, 2^12 rounds) or Argon2 (modern, resistant to GPU/ASIC attacks).
